question: Which quantity changes due to an unbalanced force?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Velocity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Newton’s Second Law of Motion**: This fundamental principle of physics states that the **acceleration** of an object is produced when an **unbalanced force** acts on it. The magnitude of the acceleration is directly proportional to the **net force** and inversely proportional to the **mass** of the object (represented by the formula **F = ma**).
 
• **Unbalanced Force**: A force is considered **unbalanced** when the **resultant** or **net force** acting on an object is not **zero**. Unlike balanced forces, which cancel each other out, an unbalanced force causes a change in the object's **state of motion**.
 
• **Change in Velocity**: Since **acceleration** is the rate of change of **velocity** over **time**, the presence of a net unbalanced force ensures that the **velocity** must change. **Velocity** is a **vector quantity**, which means it includes both **magnitude (speed)** and **direction**.
